properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From Anthony's VS Code work log (SOURCE: art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05, entry of 2026-10-01, "Later the same day", reflow2 0.76.0), in its words: "The project's PreToolUse safety hook matches on command *text*, so `--call` arguments whose prose mentions a remote-shell word are refused before they run. Workaround that worked every time: put the JSON in a file and pass `--args - < file`. A `--args @file` form would make this the obvious path."

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, so it is not re-opened:
- `--args -` reads the object from stdin, so `--args - < file` works today. The reporter used it every time. The 2026-10-02 triage measured the file route passing both a word-matching guard and an executable-position guard (fact:root-cause-a-text-matching-guard-blocks-door-writes-that-mention-remote-shell-words-and-reflow2-ships-no-such-hook-2026-10-02).
- The same triage named an `@file` form as something reflow2 could own, and left it undecided (fact:root-cause-door-prose-passes-two-quoting-layers-and-args-stdin-removes-the-shells-only-with-a-quoted-delimiter-2026-10-02).
- Checked 2026-10-05 on main (0.78.0 binary): `--help` documents only an inline object or `-`. No `@` form exists.

THE OPEN PART is whether a named-file form is worth a second spelling.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) `--args @PATH`, and the same on `reflow2 read|write TOOL @PATH`: read the object from that file. A JSON object starts with `{`, so a leading `@` cannot be mistaken for inline JSON. curl and many other command-line tools use this convention.
(b) `--args-file PATH`, a separate flag: the same effect, more explicit, no special character.
(c) NOTHING NEW IN THE BINARY: the served door instructions (req:init-installs-the-terminal-route-for-vs-code-and-update-keeps-it-current) teach `--args - < file` as THE way to pass prose, with the quoted-delimiter rule for a heredoc.

SIZE: small. A few lines where `--args` is parsed, `--help`, one test, and a line in the door instructions. No tool or schema change.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept beside it:
- It is a second spelling of something that works today. Every spelling is one more thing the served instructions must teach and keep current.
- It does not fix the guard. A guard that matches words is the user's or the organisation's, and the measured fix for that class is a guard that parses the executable position. A file only routes around it.
- A file written for one call is one more file to clean up, or to leave behind with design prose in it.
- In favour, NOT ESTABLISHED: a shell without input redirection (PowerShell reserves `<`) or a terminal tool that refuses redirects could still pass a path. Nobody has measured either on the door.
properties.name: OPEN — should the door read its arguments from a named file (`--args @file`), so design prose reaches a call with no shell quoting and never enters the command text a guard hook reads?
